description: Embedding Atlas is a tool that provides interactive visualizations for large embeddings. It allows you to visualize, cross-filter, and search embeddings and metadata.

summary.one_liner: Embedding Atlas is an interactive tool for visualizing, cross-filtering, and searching large embedding datasets along with their tabular metadata.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a tool for exploring large embeddings with automatic clustering and labeling, kernel density estimation with density contours, and order-independent transparency so overlapping points render clearly. It offers real-time search and nearest-neighbor lookup from a query or an existing point, and it is said to handle up to a few million points using WebGPU. For any tabular data, it provides linked dashboards with standard charts (bar, line, bubble, count plot, eCDF) and a composable chart spec for custom charts such as heatmaps, and charts can be set to cross-filter. It includes viewers for text, image, audio, numeric, categorical, and time columns, and AI agents can access it via MCP to query the schema, run SQL, create charts, and take screenshots. It can be run as a Python command-line tool, a Jupyter/Python notebook widget, or an npm package with React and Svelte bindings.
use_cases: find nearest neighbors to a data point
inspect text, image, or audio columns alongside embeddings
give AI agents SQL and chart access to a dataset
stack: npm package with React and Svelte bindings
notable: Automatic clustering and labeling of embedding projections
Composable chart spec for custom charts like heatmaps
MCP access so AI agents can query schema, run SQL, and capture screenshots
Usable as a CLI, Jupyter widget, or npm component library
caveats: Scale claim is 'up to a few million points', and rendering relies on WebGPU
README does not state platform or browser requirements beyond WebGPU
Demo and full documentation are on external sites not detailed in the README
